fun_facts: Ja'Marr Chase’s listed birthplace is Harvey, Louisiana.
In 2019, Ja'Marr Chase won the Biletnikoff Award, given to college football’s top receiver.
In 2019, Ja'Marr Chase recorded 1,780 receiving yards and 20 touchdowns at LSU.
Ja'Marr Chase set a Super Bowl-era NFL rookie record with 1,455 receiving yards in 2021.
Ja'Marr Chase holds the NFL rookie single-game receiving record with 266 yards, set against the Chiefs.

excerpts:
In his 2019 season at LSU, Chase dropped 4.8% of his targets, according to ESPN Stats & Information, which was just under the average for Power Five wide receivers. That year, he led that group in receiving yards and touchdowns and was given the Biletnikoff Award, which goes to the best receiver in college football.

However, the transition hasn't been as smooth for Chase since arriving in Cincinnati. He failed to catch four of his five targets in the preseason, including quarterback [Joe Burrow](https://www.espn.

excerpts:

Since Miles' comments, all Chase has done is have one of the most prolific seasons in college history (84 catches, 1,780 yards, 20 TDs in 2019) and set multiple NFL rookie records.

Chase set the Super Bowl-era rookie record in 2021 with 1,455 receiving yards, soaring past [Justin Jefferson](https://www.nfl.com/players/justin-jefferson/) 's 1,400 set the season prior. Chase added 13 TDs on 81 catches.

The 21-year-old also owns the single-game rookie record for receiving yards (266), which came in Week 17 against the Chiefs.
